summary: Repaired the Windows CI PID-marker race in the wrong-ready-version cleanup fixture: the polling helper now waits for a positive integer PID instead of treating an existing but still-empty marker file as process ID zero.

pointers: Issue#26 RED: pid marker wait ignores an empty file until a positive PID is published
M2: a wrong ready version terminates the startup path once, kills, and evicts

steps: Read the failed GitHub Actions log for PR #23 and isolated the sole failure to a cleanup assertion reporting PID 0.
Traced the fixture lifecycle: Python opens the marker file before writing its PID, while the Node helper previously returned as soon as the file existed and converted an empty read to Number('') = 0.
Added the smallest RED test with an existing empty file that later receives a positive PID; the unmodified helper returned 0 and failed as intended.
Changed only the test helper to trim, validate a safe positive integer, and keep polling otherwise; cleanup assertions and runtime behavior remain unchanged.
Re-ran the RED test together with the original wrong-ready-version cleanup test, repeated the original test five times, and completed the required full gate against the latest official DSH worktree.

evidence.target: node --test --test-name-pattern Issue#26 RED: pid marker wait tests/rlm-loop.test.ts
evidence.note: RED reproduced the race exactly: the old helper returned 0 from an existing empty marker file instead of the later-published 4242.

evidence.target: node --test --test-name-pattern Issue#26 RED: pid marker wait|wrong ready version tests/rlm-loop.test.ts
evidence.note: Both the new PID-marker contract and the original wrong-ready-version cleanup behavior passed after GREEN.
5/5 runs passed on Windows after the helper correction.

evidence.target: RLM_DSH_REPO_ROOT=upstream-latest pnpm check:upstream && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm check:memory
evidence.note: Official authority was current; typecheck/build passed; full suite reported 139 tests, 137 passed, 2 explicitly live-gated skips, and no failures; memory validation passed.
The pre-fix PR #23 run had 135 passed, 1 failed, and 2 live-gated skips; its only failure reported bad-ready-version kernel PID 0 still alive.

limitations: This candidate still requires independent review, remote CI, and merge read-back.
The change corrects a test-fixture publication race only; it does not by itself prove a live DSH Profile or M3/M4 behavior.
